prompts.system_prompt:
Your task is to revise and improve a comprehensive rebuttal package for a research paper submitted to Physical Review Letters. This includes refining the response to referee comments, the letter to the editor, the list of major changes, and the revised versions of the main paper and supplementary materials.
When revising the rebuttal package, you must: - Maintain and enhance the use of appropriate notation and terminology consistent with the field of physics. - Ensure a professional and respectful tone while strengthening the defense of the research. - Improve the specificity and detail of responses to referee comments, including more concrete examples and clearer references to changes made in the paper. - Enhance the accuracy and clarity of all mathematical equations and scientific concepts. - Refine the balance between addressing referee concerns and maintaining the integrity of the original research. - Improve the use of LaTeX formatting for all scientific notation and equations. - Further tailor the responses to the specific context of the research paper in physics. - Deepen the demonstration of understanding of the research topic and its broader implications in the field of physics.
When revising professional *.tex LaTeX documents, you must: - Enhance the use of professional LaTeX commands and environments for all scientific notation and equations. Use $\beta$, $J_1$, and $\approx$ instead of their unicode version - For quotation, prefer ``Schr\"odinger'' over "Schrodinger". Use either `` or '' as an alternative to "'. - Ensure proper use of enumerate and itemize environments for lists. - Improve overall LaTeX structure and formatting for better readability and professionalism. - When making references in the replies to the paper, use \cref{...} instead of spelled out references like "Sec.~II.C" or "Eq.~(1)".
prompts.user_prefix:
You will be revising a rebuttal package for a paper submitted to Physical Review Letters. Here are the inputs you will need:
<documents> <document name="{REPLY_TO_EDITOR_FILE}"> {REPLY_TO_EDITOR} </document> <document name="{REPLY_TO_REFEREES_FILE}"> {REPLY_TO_REFEREES} </document> <document name="{LIST_OF_MAJOR_CHANGES_FILE}"> {LIST_OF_MAJOR_CHANGES} </document> <document name="{INPUT_FILE}"> {MAIN_CONTENT} </document> <document name="{SUPP_FILE}"> {SUPP_CONTENT} </document> <document name="{EDITOR_LETTER_FILE}"> {EDITOR_LETTER} </document> <document name="{REFEREE_REPORT_A_FILE}"> {REFEREE_REPORT_A} </document> <document name="{REFEREE_REPORT_B_FILE}"> {REFEREE_REPORT_B} </document> <document name="{EXAMPLE_REBUTTAL_LETTER_FILE}"> {EXAMPLE_REBUTTAL_LETTER} </document> <document name="{INSTRUCTION_FILE}"> {INSTRUCTION} </document> </documents>
Explanation of documents: 1. Reply to Editor: The current version of the letter to the editor. 2. Reply to Referees: The current point-by-point response to referee comments. 3. List of Major Changes: The current list of significant changes made to the paper. 4. Main Paper: The current revised version of the main paper, identified by {INPUT_FILE}. 5. Supplementary Materials: The current revised version of the supplementary information. 6. Editor Decision Letter: The full text of the editor's decision and comments. 7. Referee Report A: The full text of the first referee's report. 8. Referee Report B: The full text of the second referee's report. 9. Example Reply Letter: A sample reply letter for reference. 10. Instructions: Guidelines on how to revise the reply letter.
prompts.user_request:
Please carefully review all the provided documents, including the current rebuttal package, referee reports, and example reply. Then, before revising the full rebuttal package, write out your revision plan inside the <scratchpad></scratchpad> tag. Consider how to improve each component of the rebuttal package, ensuring all referee comments are addressed more effectively and that changes to the paper are clearly communicated.
After your planning, revise the rebuttal package to include the following improvements:
1. An enhanced 1-page cover letter to the editor. Refine the summary of key points and strengthen the overall argument. Write this inside the <document name="replies/reply_to_editor.tex"></document> tag.
2. An improved point-by-point response to the referee comments. Write this inside the <document name="{REPLY_TO_REFEREES_FILE}"></document> tag. To do this: - Ensure all referee comments are accurately represented in the \begin{referee}{A} (or B) and \end{referee} environments. - Enhance each response in the \begin{response} and \end{response} environments, providing more specific details, stronger arguments, and clearer references to changes in the paper. - Improve the tone to be more respectful and diplomatic while maintaining firmness in your responses. - Strengthen the use of "They Say, I Say" principles and the "Show, not tell" approach in your rebuttals.
3. Refine the concluding paragraph for each referee to further persuade them of the paper's merits.
4. An updated and more detailed list of major changes made to the paper. Write this inside the <document name="{LIST_OF_MAJOR_CHANGES_FILE}"></document> tag. Ensure changes are clearly explained and their importance is emphasized.
5. Further revised versions of the main paper and supplementary materials that better address the referee comments and align with the improved rebuttal letter. Include specific enhancements to clarity, argumentation, and presentation.
Write the revised rebuttal package in the following format:
<rebuttal_letter> <document name="{REPLY_TO_EDITOR_FILE}"> (Insert the revised letter to the editor here, maintaining the LaTeX structure) </document>
<document name="{REPLY_TO_REFEREES_FILE}"> (Insert the revised point-by-point response to referees here, maintaining the LaTeX structure and environments) </document>
<document name="{LIST_OF_MAJOR_CHANGES_FILE}"> (Insert the revised list of major changes here, maintaining the LaTeX structure) </document>
<document name="{INPUT_FILE}"> (Insert the further revised text of the main paper here) </document>
<document name="{SUPP_FILE}"> (Insert the further revised text of the supplementary materials here) </document>
</rebuttal_letter>
Remember, the goal is to significantly improve the rebuttal package, making it more persuasive, specific, and aligned with the expectations of Physical Review Letters. Start with laying down your revision plan in the <scratchpad></scratchpad> tag. Then proceed to revising each component of the rebuttal package in the format specified above.
prompts.user_reflect:
Your revised output is still not specific enough to the paper and doesn't show sufficient improvement over the original version. After thoroughly and critically reviewing the original rebuttal package, the referee reports, and the example, write a new revised rebuttal package that satisfies the following requirements: <requirements> - Significantly increases the level of specific details, with clear and precise references to changes in the new version of the paper. - Ensures all referee comments are addressed more comprehensively, using more concrete and convincing physical arguments relevant to the paper's content. - Improves the style and tone to more closely match the provided example, while maintaining a high level of professionalism and expertise in physics. - Enhances the clarity and persuasiveness of the arguments presented in both the letter to the editor and the responses to referees. - Provides a more detailed and well-structured list of major changes, clearly linking each change to specific referee comments or overall improvement of the paper. - if any fluffy statements like "XXX provides crucial insights into the structure and behavior of these systems" or "It is important to note that..." were introduced in the revised version, they need to be condensed using the "show, don't tell" technique. - The revised version should also be self-contained and not rely on the previous version. Therefore, you cannot write "Our extended simulations now cover..." in the main text because it relies on the previous version and is not self-contained. - Physical Review Letters are very strict about the style of the paper. Therefore, you should never make any kinds of multiple line lists in the main text. - PRL has a very strict policy on the word count of the main paper. Make sure the word count of the main paper (excluding the appendix/SM) is not more than roughly 3500 words. Your added text needs to be very condensed and to the point. Otherwise you would need to condense the other parts of the paper. </requirements>
Start with laying down your revised plan in the <scratchpad></scratchpad> tag. Then proceed to output the significantly improved letter to the editor, response letter to referees, list of major changes, revised main paper, and revised supplementary materials that meet the above requirements.
